summary: Shady Sands security leader and Jarvis's brother, responsible for guard and threat information.
The Shady Sands doctor who studies and treats radscorpion poison.
Seth's younger brother and the source of the claim that an ancestor of Aradesh founded Shady Sands.
A Vault 15 survivor living at Shady Sands whose testimony preserves the Vault's crowding, schism and attack.
A former Crimson Caravan guard recuperating in Shady Sands who may accompany the Vault Dweller.
The leader of the Khans and Tandi's captor, whose autobiographical claims emphasise violent succession and trade.
Junktown's mayor, law figure and general-store proprietor, targeted for assassination by Gizmo.
The Junktown casino owner and crime boss who arranges Killian's assassination and may become the town's ruler.
The commander of Junktown's guards who can receive evidence of Gizmo's plot.
Leader of the Skulz gang in Junktown.
A Skulz associate who may leave the gang, take legitimate work and testify.
A Junktown physician implicated in an illicit trade in human remains.
A Nevada wanderer trained through a family Ranger tradition who may accompany the Vault Dweller.
A dog in Junktown who may follow the Vault Dweller; Phil supplies the limited reliable account of the dog's former companion.
The head and public figure of Far Go Traders, preoccupied with three missing caravans.
The Far Go Traders administrator who evaluates evidence from the missing-caravan investigation.
The leader of the Hub's Crimson Caravan company.
The leader of the Hub's Underground criminal network.
Decker's lieutenant and enforcer in the Underground.
The Hub police chief able to act against Decker when supplied with evidence.
The leader of the Old Town Thieves' Circle, who presents theft as redistribution amid Hub inequality.
A Hub resident and former trader whose testimony links Richard Grey's expedition, Mariposa and post-War mutation.
The ruler of Necropolis's surface ghouls, exercising local authority under constrained coexistence with Unity occupiers.
A Unity super mutant at the Watershed who captures normal humans under orders from a commander called Lou.
The leader of Necropolis's peaceful sewer community, which depends on repair of the water pump.
Founder and leader of the Followers, committed to peace and preserved knowledge while investigating the Children.
Leader of the Blades and custodian of evidence exposing the Regulator frame-up.
The public leader of Adytum, deceived about the murder of his son Josh.
The Regulator leader whose internal transmission orders Josh Zimmerman's murder and a Blades frame-up.
Jon Zimmerman's son, murdered while attempting to expose Regulator control of Adytum.
The leader of the Gun Runners and principal source for their industrial history and economic dependencies.
An Adytum chemist and technician maintaining hydroponics and equipment.
An Adytum-born thief and scavenger who may accompany the Vault Dweller and describes Boneyard faction geography.
High priest of the Children who claims partnership with the Master but is characterised by the Lieutenant as expendable.
A Cathedral official whose doctrine treats pain and obedience as instruments of enforced service.
A Followers operative infiltrating the Children and supplying access information about the Cathedral.
The Brotherhood's High Elder in 2161 and an advocate for investigating the emerging mutant threat.
The Brotherhood's Head Paladin and Master Knight, responsible for discipline and training.
The Brotherhood's Master Scribe and author of anatomical evidence concerning super-mutant reproduction.
The Brotherhood entrance guard and outsider contact who directs the Vault Dweller toward the Glow initiation task.
A Senior Paladin handling rescue, reward and military-aid matters at Lost Hills.
Vinnie's Junktown gang, socially linked to local drinking establishments and Gizmo's criminal work.
The Lars-led law force responsible for town security.
Loxley's Old Town group, which targets wealthy property and claims a redistributive purpose.
The Hub law-enforcement organisation led by Justin Greene.
The peaceful Necropolis sewer community dependent on the settlement's damaged water system.
The Hub's central merchant, caravan and civic district.
The poorer eastern Hub district and operating area of the Thieves' Circle.
The affluent western district of the Hub.
A Hub establishment serving as the Underground's operational base.
Necropolis's surface water-distribution facility, occupied by Unity mutants in 2161.
The refuge of peaceful underground ghouls and the location of the damaged pump system.
The Boneyard headquarters of the Followers of the Apocalypse.
The centre of Zimmerman and Regulator authority within Adytum.
The Blades community within the Boneyard, separated from the Gun Runners by deathclaw territory.
The Gun Runners' fixed industrial site, dependent on lathes and mills and isolated by deathclaws.
The concealed Vault beneath the Cathedral containing the Master's command centre.
The Mariposa exposure tanks used by Unity to convert captives into super mutants.
The Khans' wasteland base and site of Tandi's captivity.
